rule.description: A function or method whose body is simultaneously very large (>=60 statements) and highly branched (>=14 branch nodes) -- the structural fingerprint of sub-method implementations inlined at 3+ levels of depth, collapsing what were well-scoped helpers into a single monolithic body. Detected by a custom Pylint plugin (rule R9101, symbol deeply-inlined-method).

checks.description: Detect functions or methods whose body is large and highly branched, the structural signature of a deeply inlined method that has absorbed several well-scoped sub-method implementations.
checks.detected_relation: function body where statement count >= 60 AND branch-node count >= 14
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A method that grew to hold multiple inlined sub-responsibilities becomes both significantly larger and significantly more branched than any well-scoped method in the same codebase, because each absorbed helper contributes its own statement and control-flow nodes. Requiring both bounds to be exceeded keeps the rule specific to the deeply-inlined-method shape while excluding large-but-uniform or branched-but-trivial functions.

matches.evidence: ConfigReader._read absorbs the directory-chain traversal (formerly _recursive_read) and the per-key merge-strategy resolution (formerly _get_merge_with_stratgies, inlined twice) into a single body, reaching 61 statements and 17 branch nodes.

Stack.__init__ absorbs the boolean-coercion guard (formerly _ensure_boolean, inlined three times), the deprecated-alias field resolution (formerly _set_field_with_deprecated_alias, inlined four times), and the CloudFormation parameter casting/validation (formerly _cast_parameters) into one body, reaching 80 statements and 41 branch nodes.

excluded.reason: Template.body does dispatch into a handler-registry chain, but the chain is small and shallow once inlined, so its body stays well below the large-and-branched threshold; it is not a manifestation of the deeply-inlined-method rule and is left clean.

The deep orchestration chains in the plan/actions module are covered by test seams that patch or spy on the private helpers patch_by_patch; inlining them would alter observable behavior, so they are outside the behavior-preserving reach of this case.
